answer: The kernel multiplier is published, charged in ledge, and jade lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2246 identities would post 4022 proofs and burn roughly 60 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
